a.  Enter the data into Excel, a CSV, or JSON file. You will have some decisions to make about things like variable names, etc. Be sure to include the data set you create on your portfolio website.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import altair as alt


data = [
    {
        "survey_year": "2016",
        "total_fertility": 5.2,
        "modern_contraception_use": 38.4,
        "unmet_need_family_planning": 22.1
    },
    {
        "survey_year": "2010",
        "total_fertility": 5.4,
        "modern_contraception_use": 23.6,
        "unmet_need_family_planning": 22.3
    },
    {
        "survey_year": "2005",
        "total_fertility": 5.7,
        "modern_contraception_use": 17.6,
        "unmet_need_family_planning": 24.3
    },
    {
        "survey_year": "1999",
        "total_fertility": 5.6,
        "modern_contraception_use": 15.6,
        "unmet_need_family_planning": 22.3
    },
    {
        "survey_year": "1996",
        "total_fertility": 5.8,
        "modern_contraception_use": 11.7,
        "unmet_need_family_planning": 26.0
    },
    {
        "survey_year": "1992",
        "total_fertility": 6.2,
        "modern_contraception_use": 5.9,
        "unmet_need_family_planning": 27.8
    }
]


tanzania = pd.DataFrame(data)



```

b.  Use these data to create a visualization that tells a story. Notice that some of the surveys were conducted all in one year and some spanned two calendar years. How will you deal with that in your visualization?

```{python}
line_plot = alt.Chart(tanzania).mark_line(strokeWidth=3).encode(
    x=alt.X('survey_year', title='Survey Year', axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0)),
    y=alt.Y('total_fertility', title='Total Fertility Rate'),
    color=alt.value('pink')
).properties(
    title='Total Fertility Rate Over Time',
    width=200 
)

scatter_modern_contraception = alt.Chart(tanzania).mark_circle().encode(
    x=alt.X('total_fertility', title='Total Fertility Rate'),
    y=alt.Y('modern_contraception_use', title='Modern Contraception Use (%)'),
    color=alt.value('darkblue')
).properties(
    title='Correlation of Fertility Rate and Modern Contraception Use'
)

scatter_unmet_need = alt.Chart(tanzania).mark_circle().encode(
    x=alt.X('total_fertility', title='Total Fertility Rate'),
    y=alt.Y('unmet_need_family_planning', title='Unmet Need for Family Planning (%)'),
    color=alt.value('skyblue')
).properties(
    title='Correlation of Fertility Rate and Family Planning Needs'
)


combined_plot = alt.concat(line_plot, scatter_modern_contraception, scatter_unmet_need, spacing=20)

combined_plot
```

c.  Write a few sentences explaining the story told.

The “Total Fertility Rate Over Time” graph shows a steady decline in fertility rates from about 6 children per woman in 1992 to just above 4 children per woman by 2016. The “Total Fertility Rate vs Modern Contraception Use” scatter plot suggests a correlation between the increase in modern contraception use and the decrease in total fertility rates. The third scatter plot shows a positive correlation between the Total Fertility Rate and the Unmet Need for Family Planning. As the fertility rate increases, there is a noticeable rise in the unmet need for family planning services. This suggests that in areas with higher birth rates, there may be a greater demand for, but less access to, effective family planning methods. The plot combined illustrate how family planning and contraception have likely played a role in lowering fertility rates over the surveyed years.
